audit.why: Both layers and the packet agree on Katarina 7/7 and it matches the 53.89% win rate. Zoe has no dash — Portal Jump is a two-way blink that forces her back to the cast position — so a landed Shunpo sticks.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sleepy Trouble Bubble is described as a 20-second and '20-plus seconds early' cooldown in three separate fields. It is 18 seconds at rank 1 and 14 at rank 5.
audit.why: The entire matchup is scheduled around that one cooldown, and the page overstates the punish window by two seconds at rank 1 and by six at rank 5 — always in the direction that gets the player killed.
audit.corrected: Corrected to 18 seconds at rank 1, 14 maxed, everywhere it appears.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two kit facts are missing. Sleepy Trouble Bubble reduces the target's magic resist while asleep AND doubles the first source of damage that breaks it — the page says only 'sleep into empowered Q'. And More Sparkles! is an auto-attack reset: her combo opens with a basic attack wind-up, which is the real tell.
audit.why: enemyKit E text states the MR reduction and the doubled break damage; enemyKit P carries the autoReset flag and its text confirms the empowered basic after a spell cast.
audit.corrected: Both stated in breakdown.cooldowns and the Do's.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT); dosFull[2].d invents a 'fifteen-second' bubble window.
audit.why: The kit gives Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18s at rank 1, Paddle Star! 8.5s down to 6.5s, and Portal Jump 11/8/5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fifteen lint findings, eleven of them MISGENDER: Zoe is called 'he/his' in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, breakdown.trading, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[1].t, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].t and four report entries.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists zoe as female; the owner is addressed as 'you', so every third-person pronoun on the page refers to Zoe.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d is tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d is tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED). The packet also flags four truncated ability names: 'Paddle Star' and 'Paddle Star's' (it is Paddle Star!), 'More Sparkles' (More Sparkles!) and 'Portal Jump's' — the last is correct as a possessive.
audit.why: The exclamation mark is part of the ability name in Riot's data for both Q and the passive.
audit.corrected: Bullets rewritten to their titles; names corrected where they appear in writable prose.

edits.before: His combo is scheduled, yours is improvised — dance the daggers around his rotation and reset through the gap.
edits.after: Her combo is scheduled, yours is improvised — dance the daggers around her rotation and reset through the gap.

edits.before: Be where his combo wasn't, and blend where his cooldowns are. Sleepy Trouble Bubble is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Be where her combo wasn't, and blend where her cooldowns are. Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 18 seconds at rank 1 — that is the clock this lane runs on.

edits.before: Zoe wins by landing Sleepy Trouble Bubble, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Zoe wins by landing one bubble: the sleep cuts your magic resist and doubles the first hit that wakes you, which is her whole kill.

edits.before: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades his aim can't follow.
edits.after: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades her aim can't follow.

edits.before: Good trade: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades his aim can't follow. Bad trade: Shunpo onto a face with the CC still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.
edits.after: Good trade: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades her aim can't follow. Bad trade: Shunpo onto a face with the bubble still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.

edits.before: - Zoe Sleepy Trouble Bubble: matchup-defining — Sleep into empowered Q is the entire kill pattern — body-block it with minions or terrain. Check it before every step-up. - E Shunpo (second use) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 18s at rank 1 and 14s maxed. Asleep, your magic resist drops and the first hit that wakes you is doubled — that is the entire kill, not the Q by itself. - Paddle Star! is 8.5s and only hurts if it flies a long line, so standing close blunts it. - Portal Jump is 11s but always returns her to the tile she left.

edits.before: Dance the daggers off his aim lines
edits.after: Dance the daggers off her aim lines

edits.before: Sleep into empowered Q is the entire kill pattern — body-block it with minions or terrain. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Body-block the bubble with a minion or a wall. Until it is spent you are fighting with less magic resist than your health bar suggests.

edits.before: String the cooldown gap after his combo
edits.after: String the gap after her combo

edits.before: Q the bounce, E to the landed dagger, W as you spin out — steel-routed trades his aim can't follow.
edits.after: One missed bubble is 18 seconds where she has no self-peel and no dash. That is the window the whole matchup is built on — take all of it.

edits.before: Zoe burns Sleepy Trouble Bubble on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Zoe throws the bubble into a minion — that is an 18-second invitation at rank 1 and she cannot decline it.

edits.before: That is Zoe’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: She aims the bubble where you are going, not where you are. A predictable dagger tile is the one she throws it at.

edits.before: Trade while his CC is loaded
edits.after: Trade while her bubble is loaded

edits.before: Your lotus dies to one interrupt — counting their CC before spinning is the entire skill floor of the champion.
edits.after: Watch her basic attack, not her hands: More Sparkles! empowers the auto after a cast, so the wind-up is the tell the combo has begun.

edits.before: Shunpo onto a face with the CC still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.
edits.after: The sleep ends your channel outright, and the blades that woke you land doubled on your own bar. Confirm the bubble is gone first.

edits.before: Ahead, chain it: zone Zoe off daggers, lotus every skirmish, and reset through the map — fed Katarina is a weather event.
edits.after: Ahead, take her vision away: her picks start with a bubble thrown from fog. Ward the chokes, walk the open ground, and she never opens.

edits.before: Carry through chain reactions — one kill is three; your job is the first domino and the discipline to wait for it.
edits.after: Carry by killing her first in every fight. She has no dash and one 18-second answer; once she is down her team has no burst left to fear.

edits.before: If Zoe gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Sleepy Trouble Bubble extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q bounces and stay relevant through reset potential.
edits.after: A fed Zoe kills you from one bubble, and picking up your Flash or Ignite with Spell Thief makes it worse. Farm behind the wave so the bubble has to pass a body, and stop giving her summoner spells to collect.

edits.before: You are the cleanup that starts fights: enter on steel, lotus the clump, reset through the kill, and exit through the panic.
edits.after: You open on her, not on the fight. She stands still to aim, has no escape but a blink that returns her, and dies before the Q finishes travelling.

edits.before: Level 2 Kat's Q-E trade sticks to a dashless Zoe whose only answer is a 20s-cooldown bubble.
edits.after: Level 2 Kat's Q-E trade sticks to a dashless Zoe whose only answer is an 18-second bubble.

edits.before: Her R is a fixed two-way blink — she MUST return to where she cast it. Hold your Shunpo, let her Portal Jump in for the Paddle Star angle, then E onto the return spot and start Death Lotus as she snaps back. It's a scripted kill.
edits.after: Her R is a fixed two-way blink — she MUST return to where she cast it. Hold your Shunpo, let her Portal Jump in for the Paddle Star! angle, then E onto the return spot and start Death Lotus as she snaps back. It's a scripted kill.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 you can play aggressive: her Paddle Star Q needs to travel away and redirect back for real damage, so standing close to her actually blunts it, and Kat thrives at point-blank. Walk her down when bubble E is on cooldown — it's her only self-peel and at 20-plus seconds early, the punish window is enormous. Just respect the W summoner-spell drops; a picked-up Flash or Ignite changes her kill math.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 you can play aggressive: Paddle Star! deals more the longer it flies in a straight line, so standing close to her blunts it outright, and Kat thrives at point-blank. Walk her down when the bubble is on cooldown — it's her only self-peel, and at 18 seconds at rank 1 the punish window is enormous. Just respect the Spell Thief drops; a picked-up Flash or Ignite changes her kill math.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 the pattern is simple: make her burn Sleepy Trouble Bubble on a minion-blocked angle or Shunpo-dodge it, then all-in with Q-E-W and Preparation resets — she has no dash and melts to your full rotation. At 6 her Portal Jump is a liability against you specifically: the forced return to her cast position means you can pre-position a dagger or hold Shunpo for the snapback and channel Death Lotus on a target that literally cannot leave. Shove waves and roam on her weak clear; if she follows, she's fighting a Kat in a side lane with no escape tool.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 the pattern is simple: make her burn Sleepy Trouble Bubble on a minion-blocked angle or dodge it, then all-in with Q-E-W and your dagger resets — she has no dash and melts to a full rotation. At 6 her Portal Jump is a liability against you specifically: the forced return to her cast position means you can pre-position a dagger or hold Shunpo for the snapback and channel Death Lotus on a target that literally cannot leave. Shove and roam on her weak clear; if she follows, she is fighting a Kat with no escape tool.

edits.before: Sidestep or Shunpo-dodge Sleepy Trouble Bubble, then immediate all-in on the 20s cooldown
edits.after: Sidestep Sleepy Trouble Bubble, then all-in inside its 18-second cooldown

edits.before: Bubble-into-empowered-Paddle Star picks when you walk up to daggers predictably
edits.after: Bubble into a doubled wake-up hit when you walk to daggers predictably

notes: Charts already agreed at Katarina 7/7 across both layers and match the packet, so no chart edits were made. Eleven MISGENDER findings: Zoe was called he/his throughout. I fixed every one that lives in a sweep-scope field. FOUR REMAIN UNFIXED AND NEED THE QA PASS: report[0].t, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[9].t and report[11].t are all misgendered, but the brief caps report[] rewrites at two per matchup and I judged the pronoun swaps in the sweep fields more valuable. These five are pure one-word swaps ('His'->'Her', 'his'->'her') and should be applied wholesale rather than counted against the report budget. Fixed a wrong cooldown repeated in three fields: Sleepy Trouble Bubble is 18s at rank 1 and 14s maxed, not '20s' or '20-plus seconds early'. Also killed the invented 'fifteen-second' window. Surfaced what the page never said: the sleep reduces your magic resist AND doubles the first damage that breaks it, so the danger is not the Q alone — and More Sparkles! is an auto-attack reset, making her basic-attack wind-up the real combo tell. Removed 'Preparation resets' from mid: there is no ability called Preparation in Katarina's kit. NOT asserted: enemyKit E carries a derived 'trueDamage' flag, but Riot's own text describes a magic-resist shred and a damage multiplier, not true damage — per the brief's rule I trusted the description and wrote neither. Left unverified: item names (Luden's, Gunblade, Zhonya's) in whys[5], spikes[2] and spikes[3].
